D.D-EVS-35: Per-version versioning: 0 keeps all, 1 newest only, 2 index files; config, mailcfg, git-mode, creates-only refuse 1-2; locks refuse 1.
D.D-EVS-36: Versionless content: one-record kind-5 segments cited only by the path's next version or rename; ≤16 KiB staged; per-path slot keys.
D.D-EVS-37: Committing evs processes delete replaced versionless content 60 s after commit, evacuation by ~26 h; holds keep only pre-placement content.
D.D-EVS-38: Turning versioning off keeps every version written while on; turning it on starts history there; replaced versionless versions read `collected`.
D.D-EVS-39: Format 1 reserves and refuses format-2 constructs as FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED; a repo's first push carrying one raises `repo/`'s format to 2.
D.D-EVS-40: Directory removals and ref DELETEs list versionless files below; omitted files' content ids ride the removal marker, deleted at collection.
D.D-EVS-41: git-lfs uses versionless `ur/lfs` via a standalone transfer agent; daily prunes drop objects no tip, 30-day commit or touch references.
D.D-EVS-42: New paths take versioning from creation-time rules: repo's, else network's, else versionless above 64 MiB; only writers change it later.
D.D-EVS-43: File-mode refs index in-push under `.ur-index/i1`; git-mode refs and streams share `ur/index` by companion pushes; config, mailcfg, secret repos: none.
D.D-EVS-44: Index format 1: document-level byte trigrams, Unicode 17.0.0 normalization, VByte/bitset postings, no cross-document compression, keyed shard pads, byte-exact determinism.
D.D-EVS-45: Buckets: UTC W-day windows (30, or 7-365) by signed push time; latest spans current and previous; expired roll up oldest-first.
D.D-EVS-46: Each writer appends to a staged head ≤16,208 B, sealing into ≤8 reused slots that merges absorb into bucket shards.
D.D-EVS-47: Merges and roll-ups are functions of base files; roll-ups are single lock-fenced pushes into all; readers search every bucket present.
D.D-EVS-48: Index files ≤1 MiB; erasure's CLOSURE rewrites affected files in place, same length, fresh keys; ERASE destroys old slots' keys.
D.D-EVS-49: Companion pushes: ≤1 a minute per writer on 1 KiB blocks, else every 5 minutes; backfill after 10 min unindexed.
D.D-EVS-50: Devices fetch whole index files by sync position or "search more", search only their cache, and reproduce merges, downloading mismatches.
D.D-EVS-51: Devices holding a stale all keep rolled-up buckets, masked, until it shows them, an ERASE occurs or 2W days pass.
D.D-EVS-52: Hits count only from partitions holding the document's highest version, tombstones included, masked by bucket doc tables and ERASE lists.
D.D-EVS-53: Hosts with text verify candidates; others confirm from display fields, mail's `i/` and cached bodies, else label possible, fetching nothing.
D.D-EVS-54: Possible matches rank by trigram overlap; under 3 exact hits, desktops expand terms against local vocabulary, phones by one-edit variants.
D.D-EVS-55: Query terms under 3 bytes match as whole words through boundary trigrams, and each CJK run is one substring term.
D.D-EVS-56: Hosts with text re-extract new documents and reproduce merges and roll-ups, raising `index_mismatch` naming the signer, using their own result.
D.D-EVS-57: App-host "search more" asks a designated search indexer over §6.6's RPC; it authorizes and verifies locally, fetching nothing from evs.
D.D-EVS-58: Requesters ask own indexers first, owner-bound repos only the owner's consented ones, team repos one network-scope indexer, never app hosts.
D.D-EVS-59: Request bodies are exactly 4,016 B, replies steps × 16,384 B (1 in v1), post-parse failures included, uncompressed and uncancelled.
D.D-EVS-60: Phones merge pages per doc key, newest winning; unconfirmed local hits unreturned in the checked span collapse to "not matched".
D.D-EVS-61: One record-class `directory` repo per team network: `cards` ref, per-writer streams, `ur/index`, `erasure`; readers enforce writers; always indexed, 7-day window.
D.D-EVS-62: A repo admin's DROP push (flag 256) lists dropped versions by entry hash; any admin may cancel within 7 days.
D.D-EVS-63: Drops delete only kind-1 segments and slots named solely by listed versions; statements and hashes stay; inline content awaits compaction.
D.D-EVS-64: Commit fences listed versions; the job marks live versions, verifies with a separate implementation, deletes objects over 25 h old.
D.D-EVS-65: Holds silently defer drop deletions, the drop reading, listing and billing as finished; the index and mirrors shed listed versions.
D.D-MCP-20: Search is local and query-blind: evs sees only read receipts and sync-position fetches, `more` taking every missing all object whole.
D.D-MCP-21: Search reaches only what `evs_read` reaches, naming each exclusion but `secret` repos; non-writers reading owner-bound repos deposit receipts first.
D.D-MCP-22: Hits are confirmed, possible or near, ranked by phase, latest before all, then §11.14's tiers; only `--verify fetch` fetches bodies.
D.D-MCP-23: Untrusted hits are text-free stubs unless `untrusted: include` taints the run first; `ur search` prints them after tainting ancestor runs.
D.D-MCP-24: Record logs index only their own coordination entries and run cards, one per run; hits group by agent, active first.
D.D-MCP-25: Session-bound cursors page over start-pinned ref versions in phase order until an erasure or lost read; calls return by `wait_ms`.
D.D-MCP-26: One `directory` repo per team network, created with the team and read by every admitted sidecar, is its coordination log.
D.D-MCP-27: Runs, workers and repos announce who, what and where; runs renew hourly, expiring 90 min later; repos announce unless private.
D.D-MCP-28: From format 2, announcements are signed versionless files, a card per announcing sidecar and one per repo; before, `announce` entries.
D.D-MCP-29: Directory announcement, request and decision prose is untrusted, reaching agents only via `untrusted: include`; parked devices' writes count for nothing.
D.D-MCP-30: Requests are directory stream entries with notices approvers lease; persons decide by `RepoGrant`, `EvsShare` or `ApprovalDecision`; agents' requests need endorsement.
D.D-MCP-31: Directory readers poll, not lease, the cards ref, deriving index heads; only desktops keep buckets; phones keep cards while viewing.
D.D-MCP-32: Only a person drops history, at a device, after the server's dry run and a typed confirmation; MCP only previews.
D.D-MAIL-15: `IndexerSet`-designated mail indexers provide reliable reception; `team_mail: indexers` bars undesignated `tag:mail` listeners; with none designated, any online receiver takes mail.
D.D-MAIL-16: `i/` stays the message list; search uses an `m/`-only index keyed by message id, holding subject, from, to and date.
D.D-KEYS-22: Search-index document keys derive from `ref` (RK_1), pads from per-generation `index` keys; slot-keyed repos give each index file one key.
D.D-KEYS-23: The team directory's group follows §7.9's leaves rule (1,000 leaves, then wraps); gkm hints only the signer and config writers.
D.D-SDK-21: Searching hosts sync buckets; desktops and indexers always sync all, phones and tabs at "search more" or Wi-Fi while charging.
D.D-SDK-22: `SidecarSearch` gives apps one call streaming replacing pages of state-labeled hits naming any verifying indexer, with fetch and remote progress.
D.D-SDK-23: Conditions come from apps' `SetConditions` and browsers' key-origin frame, background time from `RunBackgroundSync`; the Go core reads no platform API.
D.D-SDK-24: The page Worker searches its own IndexedDB cache, written only by the Web Lock holder; pages get hit views only.
D.D-SDK-25: Search meets 18.4's targets, measured on surrogates and Safari's wasm before M10's exit, remote ones after M10's and M8's exits.
D.D-SDK-26: App hosts ask designated search indexers at "search more", other members' after a notice; per-device mode `on`, `own` or `off`.
D.D-SDK-27: At foreground, apps send their first-choice own indexer Hello; failover waits 3 s (5 s metered), hedging only own indexers.
D.D-SDK-28: Apps use `SidecarDirectory` for the team directory and repo announcements, `SidecarApprovals` for access requests; phones fetch announcements only while viewing.
D.D-SDK-29: In-app drop history is admin-only, behind the server's dry run and a typed name; owner-bound repos need owners' consented devices.
D.D-CORE-16: Per-network sealed index caches hold no query, hit or cursor; erasure or lost access deletes the affected data at once.
D.D-CORE-17: Search-designated daemons serve remote searches on their own `Remote*` budget (4 at once, 16 queued), persisting no query or hit.
D.D-CORE-18: `claims` defaults to auto in teams, off in personal networks; a committed `.ur` widens it only after confirmation outside MCP.
D.D-CORE-19: Devices delete dropped content locally, decrypted copies included, on applying an executed drop.
D.D-PROTO-21: `SEARCH` (0x1404) and `SEARCH_RESULT` (0x1405) carry remote search to designated indexers on data or control contracts, `timeout_ms` always 10,000.
D.D-TEAM-27: Owners or Admins network-wide, or members' consented devices for their own, designate indexers by `IndexerSet`, granting nothing; none by default.
D.D-TEAM-28: `team-create`'s first Owner device creates the directory after the config's first base; `ServiceSettings.directory` holds run (auto) and worker (on) defaults.
D.D-ABUSE-8: Preservation holds defer drops silently: covered drops commit and read as finished, their deletions waiting until every covering hold ends.
D.D-TEST-12: Versionless purge ships in observe mode; deletes start after FS-64 to FS-71 pass and a clean ≥14-day, ≥10,000-candidate production soak.
D.D-TEST-13: Format 2's bytes freeze only when projected drive writes meet D-TEST-11's gate; production measuring >10% over priced holds its rollout.
D.D-TEST-14: Every search schedule checks its results against `SearchOracle`, which shares no index code, for exact desktop hits and complete candidates.
D.D-TEST-15: Every leg reproduces testdata/index/ vectors byte-for-byte under one Go toolchain, checking Unicode and x/text versions; decoders accept only canonical encodings.
D.D-TEST-16: Remote search is checked against `SearchOracle` and by relay capture: one frame-size sequence per kind, evs request logs unchanged.
D.D-TEST-17: M10's Gn-out (M6's if later) runs FS-86's directory load at 500 and 5,000 members, counted in format 2's write gate.
D.D-TEST-18: Drop deletes start after FS-89 to FS-96 pass, TLC checks I-EVS-15 and FI-27, and a clean ≥30-day, ≥200-job observe-mode soak.
D.D-PHASE-8: Format 2 is milestone M10, built on track A from M4's exit beside M6; no recURd stage waits for it.
D.D-PHASE-9: Freezing formats reserve numbers decided later formats and milestones need; format 1 reserves format 2's and the directory's at M2.
D.D-PHASE-10: Format 2 reaches production only after its final freeze, via the `format2` gate; its deletes await D-TEST-12's and D-TEST-18's soaks.
D.D-PHASE-11: The directory ships at M6 on format 1 and moves to cards, repo files and its index with M10.
D.D-PHASE-12: Drop deletes reach production only after D-TEST-18's soak, through §19.11's `format2.drop` gate in 23.9's order.
D.D-QUOTA-10: The search index counts as storage; at the limit deletes proceed, but turning it off, merges, roll-ups and builds wait.
D.D-QUOTA-11: `sidecar_abuse:` limits directory requests per sidecar (20 pending, 50 a day, 5 a run) and per target (100 pending), client-enforced.
D.D-QUOTA-12: Drops free bytes as deleted or held; at the limit, upload-free drops and cancels are maintenance pushes; cancels skip `evs_drops_per_day`.
D.D-OPS-21: P2 taskworker drop jobs, one per segment cluster, read ≤32 MB/s and delete ≤10 objects/s, pausing above 50% HDD load.
D.D-ACL-23: Approver `autogroup:dst-owner` is the destination's owner or sponsor, else an admin; default policy uses it for dial requests, ≤30 days.
D.D-ACL-24: No document widens or narrows `directory` defaults: every admitted sidecar reads; every non-read_only one writes its own paths and stream.
D.D-ACL-25: Only repo admins drop; in owner-bound repos, only the owner's consented, not-read-only devices; a lock refuses and voids drops.
D.D-TRUST-2: Invariants I-1..I-20 bind every section; a section that cannot meet one raises a Q- item.
D.D-CORE-20: Approval-capable devices revoke their member's other devices as `lost` or `compromise`: presence where they registered one, else confirmation.
D.D-TEAM-29: A page Worker's admitter, admins' included, revokes the member's Workers it sees stale-removed; so does the member's consented device.
D.D-SDK-30: Apps list and revoke the member's other devices through `SidecarApprovals`' `GetDevices`, `PreviewRevokeDevice` and `RevokeDevice`, under §5.6's rules.

Q-ABUSE-7: How does a preservation hold apply to a drop of a path's history?
(a), owner decision 184: the drop reads as finished; deletions wait silently until holds end.
Q-ACL-11: Who approves a member's request to reach another member's device, or a tagged sidecar?
(a), owner decision 180: the destination's owner or sponsor, through `autogroup:dst-owner`.
Q-EVS-10: What happens to a path's history when versioning is turned off?
(a), owner decision 158: per version, as Perforce does; history written while on stays.
Q-EVS-11: Are the search index's files always versionless?
(a), owner decision 159: always versionless, so erasing postings is real.
Q-EVS-12: Which repo kinds may hold versionless files?
(a), owner decision 160: every kind but config and mailcfg; admins may lock repos.
Q-EVS-13: How long does replaced versionless content stay?
(c), owner decision 161: purged about a minute after the replacement commits; no recovery window.
Q-EVS-14: How do git-mode refs handle large files?
(a), owner decision 162: git refs stay versioned; git-lfs in v1 on a versionless store.
Q-EVS-15: (c), owner decision 163: in v1 as format 2; format 1 reserves numbers at M2.
Q-EVS-16: Is there a default versioning rule?
(c), owner decision 164: a per-network rule, by default versionless above 64 MiB.
Q-EVS-17: Does replaced content count toward storage?
(a), owner decision 165: replaced content counts in stored bytes until purged.
Q-EVS-18: Should evs keep the newest n versions or d days?
(c), owner decision 165: never; versionless means head-only, with no field reserved.
Q-EVS-19: Should v1 ship an admin "drop history" action for a path, which owner decision 158 allows?
(b), owner decision 173: a signed repo-admin DROP on file-mode refs, in v1.
Q-EVS-20: When does a network's versioning rule take effect?
(a), owner decision 167: at a path's creation, from the rules then in force.
Q-EVS-21: How often do git-mode refs and record streams update the index on `ur/index`?
(a) on 1 KiB blocks, else (b), owner decision 172: per minute, else 5 minutes.
Q-EVS-22: Does a repo locked fully versioned (owner decision 160) keep its always-versionless index (owner decision 159)?
(b), owner decision 168: yes, through `versioning` 2, accepted only under an index root.
Q-EVS-23: Does a drop wait out a cancellable window before it deletes?
(a), owner decision 183: a 7-day window any repo admin can cancel; `now` skips it.
Q-KEYS-16: How does the team directory's group seat every admitted sidecar?
(a), owner decision 182: its own MLS group under §7.9's leaves rule.
Q-MCP-7: Should a run's title and project reach the network's coordination log without the agent claiming them?
(c), owner decision 170: `claims` defaults to `auto` in teams, `off` in personal networks.
Q-MCP-8: What does access to a worker mean in v1?
(a), owner decision 179: grants to dial the worker's announced services only.
Q-MCP-9: Which repos does the directory announce, and may a run name a repo that some members cannot read?
(b), amended, owner decision 181: repos announce by default unless private; owners can revoke.
Q-PHASE-10: Which drives run D-TEST-13's drive-write gate before format 2's bytes freeze?
(b), owner decision 174: computed from M2's price table, confirmed after the freeze.
Q-PHASE-9: Where in v1 does format 2 go, and who builds it?
(b), owner decision 169: milestone M10 beside M6, with about three more engineers.
Q-PROTO-4: Should connect keep remote search's byte totals per contract, which show roughly how many search pages ran in each contract hour?
(b), owner decision 176: marked pairs' contract bytes round up to 128 KiB multiples.
Q-SDK-6: May a phone or browser ask one of its network's indexers to search all for verified hits, instead of downloading all for possible matches?
(c), amended, owner decisions 175, 177, 178: phones ask designated indexers; none by default.
